title: Code Comments Docstrings
summary: Writes docstrings and comments that explain why the code is the way it is, and removes stale or noisy ones, without changing behavior.
description: Most comments restate the next line, and the useful ones rot after the first refactor. This skill sends the agent through a file with a different test: would a maintainer lose something if this comment vanished?
It adds docstrings to public functions, records the reasons behind surprising code, deletes comments that lie, and leaves the executable code byte for byte alone.
useWhen: A module has public functions with no docstrings
You inherited code full of comments like "increment i"
A refactor left comments that describe the old behavior
Before releasing a library whose API doc is built from docstrings
body:
# Code comments and docstrings

Comments explain why. The code already shows what.

## Steps

1. Pick the scope (a file, a folder or the diff) and detect the project's docstring style from existing code: Google or NumPy for Python, JSDoc or TSDoc for JavaScript, rustdoc, Javadoc. Follow it; do not mix styles.
2. Read each function fully before writing about it. For public APIs, write a docstring with: a one-line summary in the imperative, parameters, return value, raised errors, and one short example when behavior is not obvious.
3. Add a comment only where the reason is not visible: a workaround and the bug it avoids, a performance choice, a unit or invariant, a surprising order of operations, a link to a spec.
4. Check every existing comment against the code. Fix it if it is wrong, delete it if it only repeats the code, keep it if it carries a reason.
5. Convert TODOs without owner or issue into either a concrete issue reference or a deletion proposal.

## Rules

- Never change executable code, formatting or imports in the same pass.
- Do not write a docstring you cannot support after reading the body. If behavior is unclear, say "unclear" in the report and skip it.
- No commented-out code; remove it, git remembers.
- Keep comments under 3 lines; longer thoughts go to docs.

## Report

Counts of docstrings added, comments rewritten and removed, plus the places where the code itself needs renaming instead of a comment.

example.prompt: Clean up the comments in src/billing/
example.result: Added 14 docstrings (TSDoc) to exported functions. Removed 31 comments that repeated the code and 6 that described removed behavior. Added 4 why-comments, for example the 3-day grace period in prorate.ts and the Stripe rounding workaround. Suggested rename: calc2() to calculateProration(). No code changed.

faq.question: Will it change how my code behaves?
faq.answer: No. Only comment and docstring text is edited, so the diff should contain nothing else.

faq.question: Why does it delete comments?
faq.answer: A wrong or redundant comment costs readers more than no comment. Each deletion appears in the diff for you to veto.
